functions.name: noun_chunks
functions.comment: Noun chunks per text row: (id, chunk, root) -- keyword/topic candidates

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Noun-phrase extraction as a table-in-out function: each input text row explodes into **one row per noun chunk** (a base noun phrase such as 'the long road'), each with its head/root token.

**When to use:** mine candidate keywords, topics, or product/feature mentions from free text without training a model -- noun chunks are a cheap, high-recall source of 'what this text is about'.

**Input:** a `(SELECT ...)` relation passed positionally; `id := 'col'` names a passthrough key; `text :=`, `lang :=`, `model :=` pick the text column, pin the language, and override the model. **Output:** rows of `(chunk, root)` plus the optional id. Text rows with no noun chunks emit nothing; output order is not guaranteed -- add `ORDER BY` for determinism.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# noun_chunks

Extracts base noun phrases from a text column with spaCy, emitting one row per chunk. Pass the input relation positionally; `id :=` names the join key copied onto every chunk row, and `text :=`, `lang :=`, `model :=` pick the text column, pin the language, and override the model.

Each row gives the noun-phrase text and its head token (`root`). Aggregate the chunks to surface frequent topics/keywords, or join back to the source via `id :=`.

functions.name: entities
functions.comment: Named entities per text row: (id, ent_text, label, start_char, end_char)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Named-entity recognition as a table-in-out function: each input text row explodes into **one row per detected entity** (people, organizations, places, dates, money, ...) found by the spaCy NER pipeline.

**When to use:** pull structured mentions out of unstructured text -- e.g. every company named across a news corpus, or every date in a contract -- so you can aggregate, filter, or join on them.

**Input:** a `(SELECT ...)` relation passed positionally; `id := 'col'` names a passthrough key copied onto every emitted row (so you can join entities back to the source); `text :=`, `lang :=`, and `model :=` select the text column, pin the language, and override the model. **Output:** rows of `(ent_text, label, start_char, end_char)` plus the optional id. Text rows with no entities emit nothing; output order is not guaranteed -- add `ORDER BY` for determinism.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# entities

Runs spaCy named-entity recognition over a text column, emitting one row per entity span. Pass the input relation positionally and name the join key with `id :=` so every emitted entity carries the source row's id; `text :=`, `lang :=`, and `model :=` choose the text column, pin the language, and override the model.

Each output row carries the entity text, its type label (`PERSON`, `ORG`, `GPE`, `DATE`, `MONEY`, ...), and the character span within the source. Rows with no entities produce no output; add an `ORDER BY` for deterministic order.

functions.name: sentiment
functions.comment: Sentiment score in [-1, 1] (VADER lexicon; tuned for English/social text)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Score the sentiment of each text with VADER and return the **compound** value in `[-1, 1]`, where `-1` is maximally negative, `0` neutral, and `+1` maximally positive.

**When to use:** rank or aggregate opinion in reviews, comments, tweets, and other short social/English text -- e.g. `avg(nlp.sentiment(body))` per product.

**Input:** one `VARCHAR` column. **Output:** a `FLOAT` in `[-1, 1]`. NULL/empty input yields NULL. VADER is a lexicon-and-rules model tuned for English and social media; it understands emphasis, negation, and emoticons but is not a translator -- score non-English text only after detecting/translating it.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# sentiment

Returns the VADER compound sentiment score in `[-1, 1]` for each text. A typical use is per-group opinion tracking -- e.g. the average `nlp.sentiment(body)` per product, so you can rank which products reviewers feel best about.

VADER is purpose-built for English social text (handling negation, intensifiers, and emoji). For a coarse neg/neu/pos bucket instead of a number, use `nlp.sentiment_label`.

vgi.example_queries.description: Score the sentiment of a literal English string
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT nlp.main.sentiment('I absolutely love this, it is fantastic!') AS score

functions.name: detect_lang
functions.comment: Detect the dominant language of each text (ISO-639 code, fastText lid.176)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Identify the dominant natural language of each input string and return its two-letter ISO-639-1 code (`en`, `fr`, `de`, `es`, ...), using the fastText `lid.176` model.

**When to use:** routing mixed-language corpora, filtering a table down to one language before applying English-only models (e.g. VADER sentiment), or building a language histogram with `GROUP BY`.

**Input:** one `VARCHAR` column. **Output:** a `VARCHAR` ISO-639 code. NULL or empty input yields NULL. Very short or ambiguous strings can be misclassified -- pair with `detect_lang_conf` and threshold on confidence when accuracy matters.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# detect_lang

Returns the ISO-639-1 language code of each text value, computed with the fastText `lid.176` identifier -- for example `fr` for `Bonjour le monde` and `en` for a plain English sentence.

Use it to segment a multilingual column before language-specific processing. Combine with `nlp.detect_lang_conf` to discard low-confidence guesses; very short snippets are inherently hard to classify.

vgi.example_queries.description: Identify the language of a literal string
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT nlp.main.detect_lang('The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog') AS lang

tags.vgi.title: Detect Language Code

arguments.name: text
arguments.description: Text column to identify

examples: SELECT nlp.main.detect_lang('The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog') AS lang

functions.name: detect_lang_conf
functions.comment: Confidence (0-1) of the detected language (fastText lid.176)

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Return the fastText `lid.176` confidence (roughly 0-1) for the **top** language guess of each input string -- the companion probability to `detect_lang`.

**When to use:** gate downstream processing on identification quality, e.g. keep only rows the model is sure about with `WHERE nlp.detect_lang_conf(body) > 0.8`.

**Input:** one `VARCHAR` column. **Output:** a `FLOAT`. NULL/empty input yields NULL. Edge case: fastText occasionally reports a confidence marginally above 1.0 (e.g. ~1.00001), so do not assert a strict `<= 1.0` upper bound on the result.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# detect_lang_conf

Returns how confident the fastText `lid.176` model is in the language it picked for each text -- a float near the `[0, 1]` range. A common pattern is to keep only confidently-identified rows by filtering on `nlp.detect_lang_conf(body) > 0.8`.

Use alongside `nlp.detect_lang`. Note the confidence can read slightly above 1.0 for some inputs, so avoid a strict upper-bound assertion.

vgi.example_queries.description: Confidence of the top language guess for a literal string
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT nlp.main.detect_lang_conf('The quick brown fox') AS conf

tags.vgi.title: Detect Language Confidence Score

functions.name: strip_stopwords
functions.comment: Remove stop-words and punctuation, returning the rest joined; language auto-detected

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Drop stop-words and punctuation and return the surviving tokens space-joined, loading a **named** spaCy model rather than the language default.

**When to use:** when a particular model is required -- a larger/transformer model for better tokenization, or a non-default model already installed in the worker.

**Inputs:** a `VARCHAR` text column, an ISO-639 `lang` (`''` ignores it when a model is given), and a `model` name. **Output:** a `VARCHAR` of the kept tokens. NULL/empty text yields NULL. The named model must be installed in the worker's environment or the call errors at load time.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# strip_stopwords(text, lang, model)

Removes stop-words and punctuation using an explicitly named spaCy model -- for instance `en_core_web_sm` for English, or a larger model already installed in the worker.

The model must be present in the worker's Python environment. When `lang` is empty the model name alone selects the pipeline.

functions.name: normalize
functions.comment: Normalize text: Unicode NFKC, lowercase, and collapse whitespace

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Canonicalize each text into a comparable form: apply Unicode **NFKC** normalization, casefold (aggressive lowercase), and collapse all runs of whitespace to single spaces (trimming the ends).

**When to use:** before equality joins, deduplication, or grouping on free-text keys so that visually-identical strings differing only in case, full/half-width forms, ligatures, or spacing compare equal.

**Input:** one `VARCHAR` column. **Output:** a normalized `VARCHAR`. NULL input yields NULL. This function is **pure Python** -- no spaCy/fastText model is loaded -- so it is the cheapest function in the worker and always available.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
# normalize

Returns a canonical form of each text: Unicode NFKC + casefold + whitespace collapse -- e.g. `  Cafe   DELUXE  ` becomes `cafe deluxe`.

Use it to make free-text keys join and group reliably. Unlike the other cleaners this needs no model, so it runs everywhere with no setup.

vgi.example_queries.description: Canonicalize a messy literal string for dedup / matching
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT nlp.main.normalize('  Café   DELUXE	—  ') AS canonical

Bucket each text into a coarse three-way sentiment **label** -- `neg`, `neu`, or `pos` -- by thresholding the VADER compound score.

**When to use:** when you want a categorical opinion bucket for `GROUP BY` / filtering rather than a continuous number; cheaper to read in dashboards than the raw score.

# sentiment_label

Returns a coarse sentiment class -- `neg`, `neu`, or `pos` -- derived from the VADER compound score by thresholding at +/-0.05. A common use is to tally how many reviews fall into each `nlp.sentiment_label(body)` bucket for a dashboard.

Use this when a label is more convenient than the numeric `nlp.sentiment` score, for example to tally how many reviews fall into each mood bucket.

workers.title: OData v2/v4 Reader
workers.tagline: Query OData v2/v4 services as tables in DuckDB (Go)
workers.summary: Query OData v2/v4 services and return their entities as rows
workers.doc_md:
# OData v2/v4 Reader for DuckDB

**Query any OData v2 or v4 REST service directly in SQL** — discover its entity sets, read entities as rows, and inspect `$metadata`, all without writing a line of HTTP or JSON-parsing code.

OData (the Open Data Protocol) is the JSON-over-REST standard behind a huge slice of enterprise data: Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Dataverse, SAP Gateway (S/4HANA and NetWeaver), Microsoft Graph, and countless in-house APIs all speak it. This extension turns those services into queryable tables, so analysts and data engineers can join live OData entities against the rest of their warehouse using plain SQL. It is a *generic* OData reader, not a vendor-specific connector, so the same three functions work against TripPin, Northwind, Dynamics, SAP, or any spec-compliant service.

Under the hood the worker speaks OData over HTTP using only the Go standard library — no heavyweight SDK — and streams results to DuckDB over Apache Arrow. It transparently follows server-driven paging (the v4 `@odata.nextLink` and the v2 `d.__next` cursor), pushes `$filter`, `$select`, `$orderby`, and `$top` down to the service so the server does the work, and understands both response shapes: v4 (`value` / `@odata.nextLink`) and v2 (`d.results` / `d.__next`). Protected services are supported via an optional bearer token argument.

The `main` schema exposes a small set of read functions covering the whole workflow: discovering the entity sets a service advertises in its service document, reading an entity set as rows of raw JSON (with `$filter`/`$select`/`$orderby`/`$top` pushdown, automatic nextLink paging, and a configurable row cap), and parsing an entity type's properties and EDM types from its `$metadata` (EDMX) document — namespace-agnostically across both EDM 3.0 (v2) and EDM 4.0 (v4). It also ships a browsable registry of well-known auth-free public services so you can start querying without a URL in hand. The catalog's executable examples and per-object example queries provide ready-to-run SQL, and the usual path is discover → inspect → read.

## Learn more

- [OData protocol homepage](https://www.odata.org)
- [OData official documentation](https://www.odata.org/documentation/)
- [Microsoft OData documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/odata/)
- [vgi-odata source code](https://github.com/Query-farm/vgi-odata)
- [vgi-go SDK](https://github.com/Query-farm/vgi-go)

example_queries.description: Discover the entity sets the TripPin OData service exposes.
example_queries.sql: SELECT name FROM odata.main.odata_entity_sets('https://services.odata.org/V4/TripPinService') ORDER BY name;

example_queries.description: Read the first 5 People entities and pull a field out of the raw JSON.
example_queries.sql: SELECT seq, json_extract_string(entity, '$.FirstName') AS first_name FROM odata.main.odata_query('https://services.odata.org/V4/TripPinService', 'People', top := '5') ORDER BY seq;

example_queries.description: Inspect the properties and EDM types of the Person entity type from $metadata.
example_queries.sql: SELECT property, type FROM odata.main.odata_metadata('https://services.odata.org/V4/TripPinService') WHERE entity_type = 'Person' ORDER BY property;

## OData read functions

Functions for reading **OData v2/v4** services from SQL over Apache Arrow.

### Functions

- **`odata_entity_sets(service_url)`** — list the entity sets a service advertises in its service document.
- **`odata_query(service_url, entity_set, ...)`** — read an entity set; one row per entity as raw JSON, following nextLink paging with `$filter`/`$select`/`$orderby`/`$top` pushdown.
- **`odata_metadata(service_url)`** — parse `$metadata` (EDMX) into one row per entity-type property.

### Notes

Start with `odata_entity_sets` to discover a service, then `odata_query` to read rows; project JSON fields with `json_extract_string`. All functions accept an optional bearer token for protected services.

## odata_public_services

A curated registry of **well-known, public, authentication-free OData services** you can query immediately — no credentials, no setup.

### Overview

Every row is a real OData service root plus its protocol version and a short description. Use it as the zero-argument starting point for exploration: pick a `service_url`, then pass it to `odata_entity_sets` to see what the service exposes, `odata_metadata` to inspect an entity type's schema, or `odata_query` to read rows. Because the view is a static in-worker registry, it scans instantly and works offline even when a listed service is unreachable.

### Columns

- `name` (`VARCHAR`) — short human-friendly service name.
- `service_url` (`VARCHAR`) — the service root URL; feed it to the OData functions.
- `odata_version` (`VARCHAR`) — `v2`, `v3`, or `v4`; pass `version := 'v2'` to `odata_query` for a v2 service.
- `description` (`VARCHAR`) — what the service contains.

### Notes

The registry is a convenience sample of stable public reference services, not an exhaustive directory — this worker can query any spec-compliant OData v2/v4 endpoint, not only these.

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## odata_query

Read an **OData v2/v4 entity set** as rows of raw JSON.

### Overview

Fetches an entity set from an OData service and returns one row per entity, following `@odata.nextLink` (v4) or `d.__next` (v2) paging automatically until the set is exhausted or `max_rows` is reached.

### Result

Each row has `seq` (0-based position of the entity across all fetched pages) and `entity` (the entity's raw JSON object text). Project individual fields with DuckDB's `json_extract` / `json_extract_string`. See this function's example queries for ready-to-run SQL against the public TripPin service.

### Notes

- Push `$filter`/`$select`/`$orderby`/`$top` down to the service with the matching named arguments; `"filter"` and `"select"` must be quoted (SQL keywords).
- Pass `version := 'v2'` for OData v2 services and `token := '<bearer>'` for protected services.
- A NULL `service_url` or `entity_set` yields zero rows rather than an error.

## odata_metadata

Inspect an OData service's **`$metadata` (EDMX) schema**.

### Overview

Fetches and parses the service's `$metadata` (EDMX/CSDL) document and returns one row per entity-type property: the entity type name, the property name, and the property's EDM type. Use it to learn the shape and column types of an entity before querying it with `odata_query`.

### Result

One row per entity-type property, with `entity_type`, `property`, and `type` (the property's EDM type) columns. Filter by `entity_type` to inspect a single type. See this function's example queries for ready-to-run SQL against the public TripPin service.

### Notes

- Parsing is namespace-agnostic, so both OData v2 (EDM 3.0) and v4 (EDM 4.0) documents are supported.
- Pass `token := '<bearer>'` for protected services; a NULL `service_url` yields zero rows.

vgi.example_queries.description: Inspect the properties and EDM types of the Person entity type from the service's $metadata (EDMX) document.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT property, type FROM odata.main.odata_metadata('https://services.odata.org/V4/TripPinService') WHERE entity_type = 'Person';

## odata_entity_sets

List the **entity sets** an OData service exposes.

### Overview

Reads the service's top-level service document (the JSON `value[]` array) and returns one row per entity-set name. This is the natural first step when exploring an unfamiliar OData service.

### Result

One row per entity set, with a single `name` column. Feed any returned `name` into `odata_query` as the `entity_set` argument to read its rows. See this function's example queries for ready-to-run SQL against the public TripPin service.

### Notes

- Works against OData v2 and v4 service documents.
- Pass `token := '<bearer>'` for protected services; a NULL `service_url` yields zero rows.

workers.doc_md:
## Open-Meteo weather for DuckDB

[Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com) is a free, high-resolution weather API. This catalog wraps it
as SQL table functions so you can query weather, climate and geospatial data directly from DuckDB.

### What you can ask

Point-based **forecasts** (hourly, daily, current), **historical** reanalysis back to 1940, **air quality**, **marine** waves and swell, **flood** river-discharge, and downscaled **climate** projections. A **geocoding** search maps place names to coordinates, and an **elevation** lookup returns terrain height. Inline **decoding macros** turn raw coded columns into labels (weather code → text/emoji, wind direction → compass, AQI and UV → categories).

### Conventions

Every function takes a `latitude`/`longitude` (geocoding takes a `name`). Timestamps are always returned in UTC; a `timezone` argument only controls how daily aggregates are bucketed. Commercial customers can pass an `apikey` at ATTACH time to use the paid endpoints.

attach_options.name: apikey
attach_options.description: Open-Meteo commercial API key. Omit for the free tier. When set, requests use the customer-* API hosts.

example_queries.title: elevation_echoes_coordinate
example_queries.description: elevation() echoes the requested coordinate and adds terrain height.
example_queries.sql: SELECT latitude, longitude FROM open_meteo.main.elevation(52.52, 13.41);

example_queries.title: geocoding_resolves_place_name
example_queries.description: geocoding() turns a place name into the coordinate the weather functions want — the starting point for anyone who has a city rather than a latitude.
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, country_code FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Tokyo', count := 1);

example_queries.description: Current conditions in Berlin, weather code decoded to text.
example_queries.sql: SELECT temperature_2m, open_meteo.main.weather_code_text(weather_code) AS conditions FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_current(52.52, 13.41)

example_queries.description: Geocode a place name; its coordinates feed the forecast functions.
example_queries.sql: SELECT name, latitude, longitude FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Paris', count := 1)

example_queries.description: The usual starting point: a place name joined straight through to its current weather.
example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.temperature_2m, open_meteo.main.weather_code_text(w.weather_code) AS conditions FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Paris', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_current(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

example_queries.description: A column of place names geocoded and forecast in one query, each city's days in its own local time ('auto' is resolved from each row's coordinates).
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, d.time, d.temperature_2m_max FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_daily(g.latitude, g.longitude, forecast_days := 3, timezone := 'auto') AS d ORDER BY p.city, d.time

example_queries.description: Label a forecast by joining to the code table.
example_queries.sql: SELECT f.time, w.description, w.emoji FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 1) f JOIN open_meteo.main.weather_codes w ON w.code = f.weather_code ORDER BY f.time

example_queries.description: Same, for a place named rather than located: geocode, forecast, then label.
example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, f.time, w.description, w.emoji FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Oslo', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, forecast_days := 1) AS f JOIN open_meteo.main.weather_codes w ON w.code = f.weather_code ORDER BY f.time

example_queries.description: Browse the lookup on its own — no arguments needed.
example_queries.sql: SELECT code, description, emoji FROM open_meteo.main.weather_codes ORDER BY code

example_queries.description: Hourly forecasts from successive earlier model runs, for scoring forecast skill by lead time (Berlin).
example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, temperature_2m_previous_day1 FROM open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(52.52, 13.41) ORDER BY time

example_queries.description: Next 3 days, daily buckets in the location's local time zone.
example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, temperature_2m_previous_day1 FROM open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 3, timezone := 'auto') ORDER BY time

example_queries.description: The past 7 days instead of the forecast window.
example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, temperature_2m_previous_day1 FROM open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(52.52, 13.41, past_days := 7, forecast_days := 0) ORDER BY time

example_queries.description: Imperial units (°F, mph).
example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, temperature_2m_previous_day1 FROM open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(52.52, 13.41, temperature_unit := 'fahrenheit', wind_speed_unit := 'mph') ORDER BY time

example_queries.description: Many locations in one query — coordinates supplied by a column.
example_queries.sql: SELECT c.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin', 52.52, 13.41), ('Tokyo', 35.69, 139.69)) AS c(city, lat, lon), LATERAL open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(c.lat, c.lon) AS w

example_queries.description: Hourly forecasts from successive earlier model runs, for scoring forecast skill by lead time, starting from the place name 'Berlin' instead of a coordinate.
example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Berlin', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w ORDER BY w.time

example_queries.description: A column of place names geocoded and queried in one pass.
example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

example_queries.description: Several places, each window starting at its own local midnight: 'auto' resolves the zone per row.

example_queries.description: Hourly historical/reanalysis weather (1940→present) for a coordinate over an explicit date range (Berlin).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: The main schema holds the full Open-Meteo function family. It groups point-based weather into forecast (hourly/daily/current), historical reanalysis, air-quality, marine, flood and climate-projection categories, plus two helpers: geocoding to resolve place names to coordinates and elevation to look up terrain height. All functions share one calling convention — a WGS84 latitude/longitude and named optional arguments (timezone, units, forecast_days, date ranges, model for forecast/history, models for specialist functions) — and emit UTC timestamps. Positional arguments accept columns, so use a LATERAL join over a bounded coordinates table for multi-location queries or to chain geocoding into weather. The schema also provides inline SQL decoding macros in its 'helpers' category — weather_code_text and weather_code_emoji (WMO code), wind_compass (degrees to a 16-point compass), us_aqi_category / european_aqi_category, and uv_index_category — that turn the raw coded columns into human-readable labels; call them schema-qualified, e.g. weather_code_text(weather_code).
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Open-Meteo functions

Point-based weather, climate and geospatial functions from [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com), organized into forecast, historical, air-quality, marine, flood and climate categories, plus geocoding and elevation helpers.

Every function shares one calling convention: a WGS84 `latitude`/`longitude` (geocoding takes a `name`), named optional arguments, and UTC timestamps. Positional arguments may be columns: use a bounded `LATERAL` join for several locations, or chain `geocoding(...)` directly into a weather function in one query.

### Decoding helpers

Several columns come back as raw codes. The schema's `helpers` category adds inline SQL macros that decode them — `weather_code_text` / `weather_code_emoji`, `wind_compass`, `us_aqi_category` / `european_aqi_category`, and `uv_index_category`. They expand inline (no round-trip); call them schema-qualified alongside the functions (applying, say, `weather_code_text` to the `weather_code` column). The browsable `weather_codes` view lists every WMO code with its text and emoji. See each object's example queries for runnable SQL.

vgi.example_queries.description: Current conditions in Berlin, weather code decoded to text.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT temperature_2m, open_meteo.main.weather_code_text(weather_code) AS conditions FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_current(52.52, 13.41)

vgi.example_queries.description: Geocode a place name; its coordinates feed the forecast functions.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, latitude, longitude FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Paris', count := 1)

vgi.example_queries.description: The usual starting point: a place name joined straight through to its current weather.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.temperature_2m, open_meteo.main.weather_code_text(w.weather_code) AS conditions FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Paris', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_current(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: A column of place names geocoded and forecast in one query, each city's days in its own local time ('auto' is resolved from each row's coordinates).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, d.time, d.temperature_2m_max FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_daily(g.latitude, g.longitude, forecast_days := 3, timezone := 'auto') AS d ORDER BY p.city, d.time

## weather_codes

The complete WMO 4677 weather-code table (`code`, `description`, `emoji`). Unlike the weather functions it needs no arguments, so it is directly browsable, and it is the lookup behind the `weather_code_text` / `weather_code_emoji` macros. JOIN it to a forecast's `weather_code` column, or query it on its own. See its example queries for runnable SQL.

vgi.example_queries.description: Label a forecast by joining to the code table.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT f.time, w.description, w.emoji FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 1) f JOIN open_meteo.main.weather_codes w ON w.code = f.weather_code ORDER BY f.time

vgi.example_queries.description: Same, for a place named rather than located: geocode, forecast, then label.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, f.time, w.description, w.emoji FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Oslo', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, forecast_days := 1) AS f JOIN open_meteo.main.weather_codes w ON w.code = f.weather_code ORDER BY f.time

vgi.example_queries.description: Browse the lookup on its own — no arguments needed.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT code, description, emoji FROM open_meteo.main.weather_codes ORDER BY code

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## previous_runs_hourly

Hourly forecasts from successive earlier model runs, for scoring forecast skill by lead time.

Pass `latitude` and `longitude` in WGS84 degrees. The function returns one row per hour; every timestamp is emitted in UTC. Notes: the window is set with forecast_days / past_days; units are configurable (temperature_unit, wind_speed_unit, precipitation_unit); specific models can be selected with the models argument; timezone only shifts where the window starts and how daily buckets are aligned — instants stay UTC; use timezone := 'auto' to resolve the zone from each row's coordinates; the provider holds one UTC offset across a response.

If you have a place name rather than a coordinate, resolve it with `geocoding(...)` and join its `latitude`/`longitude` straight in — the positional arguments take column references, so name → weather stays one query.

Returned columns are `time` plus `temperature_2m`, `temperature_2m_previous_day1`, `temperature_2m_previous_day2` and more — see the result schema for the full set with types. Runnable queries live in this function's example queries rather than inline here.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hourly forecasts from successive earlier model runs, for scoring forecast skill by lead time (Berlin).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, temperature_2m_previous_day1 FROM open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(52.52, 13.41) ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Next 3 days, daily buckets in the location's local time zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, temperature_2m_previous_day1 FROM open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 3, timezone := 'auto') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: The past 7 days instead of the forecast window.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, temperature_2m_previous_day1 FROM open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(52.52, 13.41, past_days := 7, forecast_days := 0) ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT c.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin', 52.52, 13.41), ('Tokyo', 35.69, 139.69)) AS c(city, lat, lon), LATERAL open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(c.lat, c.lon) AS w

vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.previous_runs_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

tags.vgi.doc_md:
## historical_hourly

Hourly historical/reanalysis weather (1940→present) for a coordinate.

Pass `latitude` and `longitude` in WGS84 degrees. The function returns one row per hour; every timestamp is emitted in UTC. Notes: a start_date/end_date range is required (yyyy-mm-dd); units are configurable (temperature_unit, wind_speed_unit, precipitation_unit); select one model with model; model_selection records that request, while retrieved_at records response retrieval, not forecast issuance; timezone only shifts where the window starts and how daily buckets are aligned — instants stay UTC; use timezone := 'auto' to resolve the zone from each row's coordinates; the provider holds one UTC offset across a response.

If you have a place name rather than a coordinate, resolve it with `geocoding(...)` and join its `latitude`/`longitude` straight in — the positional arguments take column references, so name → weather stays one query.

Returned columns are `time` plus `temperature_2m`, `relative_humidity_2m`, `dew_point_2m` and more — see the result schema for the full set with types. Decode the `weather_code` column with the `weather_code_text` / `weather_code_emoji` macros. Runnable queries live in this function's example queries rather than inline here.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hourly historical/reanalysis weather (1940→present) for a coordinate over an explicit date range (Berlin).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.historical_hourly(52.52, 13.41, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Imperial units (°F, mph).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.historical_hourly(52.52, 13.41, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07', temperature_unit := 'fahrenheit', wind_speed_unit := 'mph') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Select a model explicitly and inspect the response provenance. Retrieval time does not identify the forecast run.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m, model_selection, grid_latitude, grid_longitude, retrieved_at FROM open_meteo.main.historical_hourly(52.52, 13.41, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07', model := 'era5') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Many locations in one query — coordinates supplied by a column.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT c.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin', 52.52, 13.41), ('Tokyo', 35.69, 139.69)) AS c(city, lat, lon), LATERAL open_meteo.main.historical_hourly(c.lat, c.lon, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07') AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: Hourly historical/reanalysis weather (1940→present) for a coordinate, starting from the place name 'Berlin' instead of a coordinate.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Berlin', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.historical_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07') AS w ORDER BY w.time

vgi.example_queries.description: A column of place names geocoded and queried in one pass.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.historical_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07') AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: Several places, each window starting at its own local midnight: 'auto' resolves the zone per row.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.historical_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07', timezone := 'auto') AS w ORDER BY p.city, w.time

vgi.semantic_entity.title: Hourly historical weather
vgi.semantic_entity.description: Historical model estimates, not station observations. The best_match default can blend forecast-model and reanalysis products; select model = era5 for a consistent reanalysis product. Requires an inclusive start_date/end_date range. Hourly time grouping uses UTC.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Invocation row key
vgi.semantic_members.description: Row identity within one coordinate invocation. Driving location identifiers remain part of correlated query grain.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested latitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested WGS84 latitude in degrees north, retained per input location. This is not the provider's grid-cell coordinate.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested longitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested WGS84 longitude in degrees east, retained per input location. Use the driving site's identifier to distinguish sites sharing coordinates.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Valid time (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: UTC valid hour. Some fields describe this instant; amounts and averages can describe the preceding hour. Rollups group timestamp labels in UTC, not interval overlap. Use daily fields for provider daily totals.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Air temperature (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Air temperature at 2 metres at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Relative humidity (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Relative humidity at 2 metres at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Feels-like temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Apparent temperature accounting for wind, humidity and radiation.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly precipitation (water equivalent)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Total rain, showers and snowfall water equivalent in the preceding hour. Snowfall depth must not be added to this amount.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly new snowfall depth
vgi.semantic_members.description: New snow depth in the preceding hour, not settled snow depth or liquid-water equivalent.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Weather condition code
vgi.semantic_members.description: WMO condition code. Follow the weather_codes relationship for its description and emoji. Codes are categories, not quantities.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Sea-level pressure
vgi.semantic_members.description: Air pressure reduced to mean sea level, rather than pressure at the ground.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total cloud cover
vgi.semantic_members.description: Fraction of sky covered by clouds, expressed as a percentage.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Wind speed (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Modeled wind speed at 10 metres at the valid time; distinct from gust speed.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Wind direction (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Direction FROM which wind blows, degrees clockwise from north. Arithmetic averaging is not a valid direction average.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Dew point (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Dew-point temperature at 2 metres at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly rain including showers
vgi.semantic_members.description: Liquid precipitation including showers during the preceding hour. Archive rain differs from forecast large-scale rain.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Surface pressure
vgi.semantic_members.description: Air pressure at the modeled ground elevation; not reduced to sea level.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Modeled gust (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Modeled wind gust at the indicated hour. Temporal support varies by source model; not uniformly a preceding-hour maximum.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly mean solar irradiance
vgi.semantic_members.description: Mean global shortwave irradiance on a horizontal surface (direct plus diffuse) over the preceding hour. W/m² is power per area; do not sum it and label the result as energy.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Mean hourly temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Arithmetic mean of available hourly temperature samples at each location. Missing samples are excluded; interpolated samples can be present.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Highest hourly temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Highest available hourly temperature at each location; extremes between samples can be missed.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Lowest hourly temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Lowest available hourly temperature at each location; extremes between samples can be missed.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total precipitation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sum of selected preceding-hour water-equivalent amounts at each location. Missing hours are excluded, not dry. This is not a regional total across sites.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total new snowfall depth
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sum of new snowfall depths over the selected hourly intervals at each location, not the final snowpack depth.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Maximum wind speed
vgi.semantic_members.description: Maximum available wind-speed sample at each location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Strongest wind gust
vgi.semantic_members.description: Largest supplied gust value at each location. Its underlying interval follows the source model's gust definition.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly temperature samples available
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of non-null hourly temperature samples. This does not measure precipitation coverage, observational independence or accuracy.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly precipitation samples available
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of non-null hourly precipitation amounts, including reported zero amounts. Not the number of wet hours.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested model selection
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested model selector, or provider_default where model selection is unavailable. best_match may combine models. Even an explicit selector does not identify the source of every derived field, such as precipitation probability.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Source API product
vgi.semantic_members.description: Public API product URL, without query parameters or credentials. Commercial requests use the corresponding customer host.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Response retrieved at (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: When this worker received the upstream JSON response. Preserved on worker-cache hits. This is not a model run time, issue time or data freshness guarantee.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Returned grid latitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider-returned grid latitude, which may differ from the requested location. It does not identify every component grid in blended or derived data.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Returned grid longitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider-returned grid longitude, which may differ from the requested location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Downscaling elevation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider-returned target elevation used for location selection and downscaling, where supplied. This is not necessarily the raw model-grid elevation.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Resolved response timezone
vgi.semantic_members.description: Timezone identifier returned by the provider. Timestamps remain UTC instants; the response UTC offset labels provider daily intervals.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Response UTC offset
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider's fixed UTC offset for this response. It is not recomputed for DST transitions within the response.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Aggregation interval start (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Start of the row's nominal aggregation window. Applies only to fields assigned this window in open_meteo.temporal metadata; instantaneous values use time instead.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Aggregation interval end (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: End of the row's nominal aggregation window. Hourly/current accumulation windows end at time; daily windows start at time. Source-dependent fields have no asserted common window.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Aggregation interval length
vgi.semantic_members.description: Length of the nominal aggregation window: 3600 seconds hourly, 86400 seconds for a provider day, or the provider's current.interval. Unknown current intervals stay NULL. This is not the native model resolution.

vgi.semantic_relationships.description: Optional WMO lookup; an unknown or missing code must not remove weather rows.

## marine_hourly

Hourly marine forecast (wave/swell) for a coordinate.

Pass `latitude` and `longitude` in WGS84 degrees. The function returns one row per hour; every timestamp is emitted in UTC. Notes: the window is set with forecast_days / past_days; timezone only shifts where the window starts and how daily buckets are aligned — instants stay UTC; use timezone := 'auto' to resolve the zone from each row's coordinates; the provider holds one UTC offset across a response.

If you have a place name rather than a coordinate, resolve it with `geocoding(...)` and join its `latitude`/`longitude` straight in — the positional arguments take column references, so name → weather stays one query.

Returned columns are `time` plus `wave_height`, `wave_direction`, `wave_period` and more — see the result schema for the full set with types. Runnable queries live in this function's example queries rather than inline here.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hourly marine forecast (wave/swell) for a coordinate (Berlin).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, wave_height, wave_direction FROM open_meteo.main.marine_hourly(52.52, 13.41) ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Next 3 days, daily buckets in the location's local time zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, wave_height, wave_direction FROM open_meteo.main.marine_hourly(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 3, timezone := 'auto') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: The past 7 days instead of the forecast window.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, wave_height, wave_direction FROM open_meteo.main.marine_hourly(52.52, 13.41, past_days := 7, forecast_days := 0) ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Many locations in one query — coordinates supplied by a column.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT c.city, w.time, w.wave_height FROM (VALUES ('Berlin', 52.52, 13.41), ('Tokyo', 35.69, 139.69)) AS c(city, lat, lon), LATERAL open_meteo.main.marine_hourly(c.lat, c.lon) AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: Hourly marine forecast (wave/swell) for a coordinate, starting from the place name 'Scheveningen' instead of a coordinate.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.time, w.wave_height FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Scheveningen', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.marine_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w ORDER BY w.time

vgi.example_queries.description: A column of place names geocoded and queried in one pass.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.wave_height FROM (VALUES ('Scheveningen'), ('Brighton')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.marine_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: Several places, each window starting at its own local midnight: 'auto' resolves the zone per row.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.wave_height FROM (VALUES ('Scheveningen'), ('Brighton')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.marine_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, timezone := 'auto') AS w ORDER BY p.city, w.time

## historical_daily

Daily historical/reanalysis weather (1940→present) for a coordinate.

Pass `latitude` and `longitude` in WGS84 degrees. The function returns one row per day; every timestamp is emitted in UTC. Notes: a start_date/end_date range is required (yyyy-mm-dd); units are configurable (temperature_unit, wind_speed_unit, precipitation_unit); select one model with model; model_selection records that request, while retrieved_at records response retrieval, not forecast issuance; timezone only shifts where the window starts and how daily buckets are aligned — instants stay UTC; use timezone := 'auto' to resolve the zone from each row's coordinates; the provider holds one UTC offset across a response.

If you have a place name rather than a coordinate, resolve it with `geocoding(...)` and join its `latitude`/`longitude` straight in — the positional arguments take column references, so name → weather stays one query.

Returned columns are `time` and the calendar `date` plus `weather_code`, `temperature_2m_max`, `temperature_2m_min` and more — see the result schema for the full set with types. Decode the `weather_code` column with the `weather_code_text` / `weather_code_emoji` macros. Runnable queries live in this function's example queries rather than inline here.

vgi.example_queries.description: Daily historical/reanalysis weather (1940→present) for a coordinate over an explicit date range (Berlin).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, weather_code, temperature_2m_max FROM open_meteo.main.historical_daily(52.52, 13.41, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07') ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: Imperial units (°F, mph).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, weather_code, temperature_2m_max FROM open_meteo.main.historical_daily(52.52, 13.41, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07', temperature_unit := 'fahrenheit', wind_speed_unit := 'mph') ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: Select a model explicitly and inspect the response provenance. Retrieval time does not identify the forecast run.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, weather_code, temperature_2m_max, model_selection, grid_latitude, grid_longitude, retrieved_at FROM open_meteo.main.historical_daily(52.52, 13.41, '2024-06-01', '2024-06-07', model := 'era5') ORDER BY date

vgi.semantic_entity.title: Daily historical weather
vgi.semantic_entity.description: Historical model estimates, not station observations. The best_match default can blend forecast-model and reanalysis products; select model = era5 for a consistent reanalysis product. Requires an inclusive start_date/end_date range. Dates label the provider's fixed-offset days; DST transitions within a response are not applied.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Invocation row key
vgi.semantic_members.description: Row identity within one coordinate invocation. Driving location identifiers remain part of correlated query grain.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested latitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested WGS84 latitude in degrees north, retained per input location. This is not the provider's grid-cell coordinate.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested longitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested WGS84 longitude in degrees east, retained per input location. Use the driving site's identifier to distinguish sites sharing coordinates.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily interval start (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: UTC start instant of the provider's daily interval. Select date for the provider's calendar label; this instant is not a UTC-day aggregate.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Date in requested zone
vgi.semantic_members.description: Calendar label of the provider's daily interval in the requested zone (auto by default). The API holds one UTC offset across the response; intervals crossing a DST transition may differ from civil calendar days.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily weather condition code
vgi.semantic_members.description: Most severe WMO condition in the provider's daily interval. Follow weather_codes for readable conditions; do not average these codes.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily high temperature (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Maximum air temperature in the provider's daily interval.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily low temperature (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Minimum air temperature in the provider's daily interval.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily high feels-like temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Maximum apparent temperature in the provider's daily interval.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily low feels-like temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Minimum apparent temperature in the provider's daily interval.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Sunrise (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sunrise instant for the provider's date, in UTC. May be unavailable during polar day or night.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Sunset (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sunset instant for the provider's date, in UTC. May be unavailable during polar day or night.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily precipitation (water equivalent)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Total rain, showers and snowfall water equivalent in the provider's daily interval.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily new snowfall depth
vgi.semantic_members.description: Total new snowfall depth in the provider's daily interval; not water equivalent or final snowpack depth.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hours with precipitation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider count of wet hourly intervals in this day. This is not an exact duration of rainfall, and includes precipitation other than rain.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily maximum wind speed (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Maximum wind speed at 10 metres in the provider's daily interval.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily strongest gust (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Maximum wind gust at 10 metres in the provider's daily interval.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily dominant wind direction (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider's dominant wind direction, FROM which wind blows, clockwise from north. Do not compute arithmetic averages of angles.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily solar energy
vgi.semantic_members.description: Global shortwave solar energy on a horizontal surface (direct plus diffuse) in the provider's daily interval. Energy (MJ/m²), not irradiance (W/m²).

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily rain including showers
vgi.semantic_members.description: Liquid precipitation including showers in the provider's daily interval. Archive rain differs from forecast large-scale rain.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Highest daily high
vgi.semantic_members.description: Highest available daily high in the selected period at each location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Lowest daily low
vgi.semantic_members.description: Lowest available daily low in the selected period at each location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total precipitation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sum of available daily water-equivalent precipitation amounts at each location. Missing days are excluded, not dry; not a regional total across sites.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total new snowfall depth
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sum of new snowfall depths over selected days at each location, not final snowpack depth.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total hours with precipitation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sum of provider wet-hour counts over selected days at each location, not exact rain duration.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Strongest wind gust
vgi.semantic_members.description: Strongest reported daily gust in the selected period at each location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Days with any reported precipitation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of days with reported precipitation greater than zero. Missing values are excluded. This is not a climatological wet-day index with a fixed millimetre threshold.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daily precipitation samples available
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of days with a precipitation amount, including zero. Other variables may have different coverage.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Days with both temperature extremes
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of days where both high and low temperature are available. This does not establish coverage of other variables.

functions.name: geocoding
functions.comment: Search places by name and return their coordinates (Open-Meteo geocoding).

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Forward geocoding: search Open-Meteo's place-name database and get coordinates back. Use it to turn a name like 'Berlin' into the latitude/longitude the forecast_* and marine/air-quality functions need — the bridge from human place names to the coordinate-based weather functions. Returns up to `count` candidate places (with country, admin regions, timezone, elevation and population) ordered by relevance.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## geocoding

Search places by name and return their coordinates and metadata (country, administrative regions, timezone, elevation, population).

This is the name → coordinate bridge for the rest of the catalog: read the `latitude`/`longitude` of a match, then feed them to a `forecast_*`, `marine_*`, `air_quality_*` or `elevation` function. Both sides take column references, so the bridge is one correlated join rather than two steps — the last example query joins a column of place names straight through to current weather.

Key columns are `name`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `country` and the `admin1`–`admin4` regions; see the result schema for the full set. Runnable queries are in this function's example queries.

vgi.example_queries.description: Find places named Berlin.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, latitude, longitude, country FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Berlin')

vgi.example_queries.description: Up to 20 matches (coordinates feed the forecast_* functions).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, latitude, longitude, country FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Springfield', count := 20)

vgi.example_queries.description: Localized search restricted to one country.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT name, latitude, longitude FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('München', language := 'de', country_code := 'DE')

vgi.example_queries.description: Resolve a whole column of place names in one correlated join.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, g.name, g.latitude, g.longitude FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g

vgi.example_queries.description: The bridge itself: a place name straight through to current weather.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.temperature_2m, open_meteo.main.weather_code_text(w.weather_code) AS conditions FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Reykjavík', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_current(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: A column of place names joined through to current weather in one query.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_current(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

functions.name: forecast_hourly
functions.comment: Hourly weather forecast (up to 16 days) for a coordinate.

open_meteo.provenance.note: Regular API responses do not identify a unique run. Model-update status timestamps must not be treated as the run behind these rows. Explicit model selection can still include derived fields from auxiliary sources.

uv_index.note: UV temporal support depends on the source and solar interpolation; hourly output cadence is not proof of an instantaneous value.

precipitation_probability.note: Nominal hourly threshold; source-native calculation and interpolation can differ. Hourly probabilities are not independent and must not be summed or multiplied into a period probability.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Point weather query returning hourly values from the Open-Meteo API. Hourly weather forecast (up to 16 days) for a coordinate. Supply latitude and longitude in WGS84 degrees; it returns one row per hour, with the `time` column always emitted in UTC. Notes: the window is set with forecast_days / past_days; units are configurable (temperature_unit, wind_speed_unit, precipitation_unit); select one model with model; model_selection records that request, while retrieved_at records response retrieval, not forecast issuance; timezone only shifts where the window starts and how daily buckets are aligned — instants stay UTC; use timezone := 'auto' to resolve the zone from each row's coordinates; the provider holds one UTC offset across a response. Starting from a place name instead of a coordinate? Both positional arguments accept column references, so feed them the `latitude`/`longitude` of a `geocoding(...)` match in the same query — the example queries show that form.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## forecast_hourly

Hourly weather forecast (up to 16 days) for a coordinate.

Pass `latitude` and `longitude` in WGS84 degrees. The function returns one row per hour; every timestamp is emitted in UTC. Notes: the window is set with forecast_days / past_days; units are configurable (temperature_unit, wind_speed_unit, precipitation_unit); select one model with model; model_selection records that request, while retrieved_at records response retrieval, not forecast issuance; timezone only shifts where the window starts and how daily buckets are aligned — instants stay UTC; use timezone := 'auto' to resolve the zone from each row's coordinates; the provider holds one UTC offset across a response.

If you have a place name rather than a coordinate, resolve it with `geocoding(...)` and join its `latitude`/`longitude` straight in — the positional arguments take column references, so name → weather stays one query.

Returned columns are `time` plus `temperature_2m`, `relative_humidity_2m`, `dew_point_2m` and more — see the result schema for the full set with types. Decode the `weather_code` column with the `weather_code_text` / `weather_code_emoji` macros. Runnable queries live in this function's example queries rather than inline here.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hourly weather forecast (up to 16 days) for a coordinate (Berlin).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41) ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Next 3 days, daily buckets in the location's local time zone.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 3, timezone := 'auto') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: The past 7 days instead of the forecast window.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, past_days := 7, forecast_days := 0) ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Imperial units (°F, mph).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, temperature_unit := 'fahrenheit', wind_speed_unit := 'mph') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Select a model explicitly and inspect the response provenance. Retrieval time does not identify the forecast run.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m, model_selection, grid_latitude, grid_longitude, retrieved_at FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, model := 'gfs_global') ORDER BY time

vgi.example_queries.description: Many locations in one query — coordinates supplied by a column.

vgi.example_queries.description: Hourly weather forecast (up to 16 days) for a coordinate, starting from the place name 'Berlin' instead of a coordinate.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Berlin', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w ORDER BY w.time

vgi.example_queries.description: A column of place names geocoded and queried in one pass.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: Several places, each window starting at its own local midnight: 'auto' resolves the zone per row.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, timezone := 'auto') AS w ORDER BY p.city, w.time

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: interval_end
vgi.result_columns_schema.description: End of the row's nominal aggregation window. Hourly/current accumulation windows end at time; daily windows start at time. Source-dependent fields have no asserted common window.

vgi.result_columns_schema.name: interval_seconds

vgi.semantic_entity.title: Hourly forecast
vgi.semantic_entity.description: All returned hourly weather fields, with deliberate period measures. Use daily forecasts for the provider's daily totals and extremes.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Invocation row key
vgi.semantic_members.description: Row identity within one coordinate invocation. Driving location identifiers remain part of correlated query grain.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested latitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested WGS84 latitude in degrees north, retained per input location. This is not the provider's grid-cell coordinate.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested longitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested WGS84 longitude in degrees east, retained per input location. Use the driving site's identifier to distinguish sites sharing coordinates.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Valid time (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: UTC valid hour. Some fields describe this instant; amounts and averages can describe the preceding hour. Rollups group timestamp labels in UTC, not interval overlap. Use daily fields for provider daily totals.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Air temperature (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Air temperature at 2 metres at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Relative humidity (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Relative humidity at 2 metres at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Feels-like temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Apparent temperature accounting for wind, humidity and radiation.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly precipitation (water equivalent)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Total rain, showers and snowfall water equivalent in the preceding hour. Snowfall depth must not be added to this amount.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly new snowfall depth
vgi.semantic_members.description: New snow depth in the preceding hour, not settled snow depth or liquid-water equivalent.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Weather condition code
vgi.semantic_members.description: WMO condition code. Follow the weather_codes relationship for its description and emoji. Codes are categories, not quantities.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Sea-level pressure
vgi.semantic_members.description: Air pressure reduced to mean sea level, rather than pressure at the ground.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total cloud cover
vgi.semantic_members.description: Fraction of sky covered by clouds, expressed as a percentage.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Wind speed (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Modeled wind speed at 10 metres at the valid time; distinct from gust speed.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Wind direction (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Direction FROM which wind blows, degrees clockwise from north. Arithmetic averaging is not a valid direction average.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Dew point (2 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Modeled dew-point temperature at 2 metres at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly precipitation probability
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider probability of precipitation over the preceding hour, using a nominal 0.1 mm/hour water-equivalent threshold. Calculation can use coarser ensemble intervals and interpolation. It is not a period probability and does not necessarily come from the selected deterministic model.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly large-scale rain
vgi.semantic_members.description: Large-scale rain in the preceding hour. Convective showers are separate in forecast data; use precipitation for all precipitation types.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly maximum gust (10 m)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Maximum wind gust at 10 metres during the preceding hour.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Visibility
vgi.semantic_members.description: Modeled horizontal visibility at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: UV index
vgi.semantic_members.description: Modeled UV radiation index at this hour. Temporal support depends on the source and solar interpolation; hourly cadence does not establish an instantaneous value.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Daylight
vgi.semantic_members.description: Whether the location is in daylight at the valid time.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Mean hourly temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Arithmetic mean of available hourly temperature samples at each location. Missing samples are excluded; interpolated samples can be present.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Highest hourly temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Highest available hourly temperature at each location; extremes between samples can be missed.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Lowest hourly temperature
vgi.semantic_members.description: Lowest available hourly temperature at each location; extremes between samples can be missed.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total precipitation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sum of selected preceding-hour water-equivalent amounts at each location. Missing hours are excluded, not dry. This is not a regional total across sites.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Total new snowfall depth
vgi.semantic_members.description: Sum of new snowfall depths over the selected hourly intervals at each location, not the final snowpack depth.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Maximum wind speed
vgi.semantic_members.description: Maximum available wind-speed sample at each location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Strongest wind gust
vgi.semantic_members.description: Largest supplied gust value at each location. Its underlying interval follows the source model's gust definition.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly temperature samples available
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of non-null hourly temperature samples. This does not measure precipitation coverage, observational independence or accuracy.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly precipitation samples available
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of non-null hourly precipitation amounts, including reported zero amounts. Not the number of wet hours.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Minimum visibility
vgi.semantic_members.description: Lowest available hourly visibility at each location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Maximum UV index
vgi.semantic_members.description: Highest available hourly UV index in the selected period.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Highest hourly precipitation probability
vgi.semantic_members.description: Largest supplied hourly probability in the selected period. This is not the probability of precipitation anywhere in the whole period; hours are not independent.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Hourly probability samples available
vgi.semantic_members.description: Count of non-null hourly probabilities, including reported zero probability. This does not measure coverage of precipitation amounts.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Requested model selection
vgi.semantic_members.description: Requested model selector, or provider_default where model selection is unavailable. best_match may combine models. Even an explicit selector does not identify the source of every derived field, such as precipitation probability.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Source API product
vgi.semantic_members.description: Public API product URL, without query parameters or credentials. Commercial requests use the corresponding customer host.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Response retrieved at (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: When this worker received the upstream JSON response. Preserved on worker-cache hits. This is not a model run time, issue time or data freshness guarantee.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Returned grid latitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider-returned grid latitude, which may differ from the requested location. It does not identify every component grid in blended or derived data.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Returned grid longitude
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider-returned grid longitude, which may differ from the requested location.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Downscaling elevation
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider-returned target elevation used for location selection and downscaling, where supplied. This is not necessarily the raw model-grid elevation.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Resolved response timezone
vgi.semantic_members.description: Timezone identifier returned by the provider. Timestamps remain UTC instants; the response UTC offset labels provider daily intervals.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Response UTC offset
vgi.semantic_members.description: Provider's fixed UTC offset for this response. It is not recomputed for DST transitions within the response.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Aggregation interval start (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: Start of the row's nominal aggregation window. Applies only to fields assigned this window in open_meteo.temporal metadata; instantaneous values use time instead.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Aggregation interval end (UTC)
vgi.semantic_members.description: End of the row's nominal aggregation window. Hourly/current accumulation windows end at time; daily windows start at time. Source-dependent fields have no asserted common window.

vgi.semantic_members.title: Aggregation interval length
vgi.semantic_members.description: Length of the nominal aggregation window: 3600 seconds hourly, 86400 seconds for a provider day, or the provider's current.interval. Unknown current intervals stay NULL. This is not the native model resolution.

arguments.name: longitude
arguments.description: Longitude in degrees east (WGS84).

arguments.name: forecast_days
arguments.description: Number of forecast days to return.

arguments.name: model
arguments.description: One Open-Meteo model selector (default best_match). For example, gfs_global selects the GFS product. This records a requested selection, not the resolved source or model run of every variable. Comma-separated lists are not supported.

arguments.name: past_days
arguments.description: Number of past days to include.

arguments.name: precipitation_unit
arguments.description: Precipitation unit for the response.

arguments.name: temperature_unit
arguments.description: Temperature unit for the response.

arguments.name: timezone
arguments.description: IANA timezone or 'auto'. Daily intervals use the provider's fixed UTC offset for this zone; DST transitions within a response are not applied. Time columns are always emitted as UTC. 'auto' resolves from each row's own coordinates, so under a LATERAL join every location gets its local zone. Daily functions default to 'auto'; other functions default to GMT. The value must be a constant — a named argument cannot read a column.

arguments.name: wind_speed_unit
arguments.description: Wind-speed unit for the response.

examples: SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41) ORDER BY time
SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 3, timezone := 'auto') ORDER BY time
SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, past_days := 7, forecast_days := 0) ORDER BY time
SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, temperature_unit := 'fahrenheit', wind_speed_unit := 'mph') ORDER BY time
SELECT time, temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m, model_selection, grid_latitude, grid_longitude, retrieved_at FROM open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(52.52, 13.41, model := 'gfs_global') ORDER BY time
SELECT c.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin', 52.52, 13.41), ('Tokyo', 35.69, 139.69)) AS c(city, lat, lon), LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(c.lat, c.lon) AS w
SELECT g.name, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Berlin', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w ORDER BY w.time

SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w

SELECT p.city, w.time, w.temperature_2m FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.forecast_hourly(g.latitude, g.longitude, timezone := 'auto') AS w ORDER BY p.city, w.time

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Point weather query returning daily values from the Open-Meteo API. Daily river-discharge / flood forecast for a coordinate. tags.vgi.doc_md:
## flood_daily

Daily river-discharge / flood forecast for a coordinate.

Pass `latitude` and `longitude` in WGS84 degrees. The function returns one row per day; every timestamp is emitted in UTC. Notes: the window is set with forecast_days / past_days.

If you have a place name rather than a coordinate, resolve it with `geocoding(...)` and join its `latitude`/`longitude` straight in — the positional arguments take column references, so name → weather stays one query.

Returned columns are `time` and the calendar `date` plus `river_discharge` and more — see the result schema for the full set with types. Runnable queries live in this function's example queries rather than inline here.

vgi.example_queries.description: Daily river-discharge / flood forecast for a coordinate (Berlin).
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, river_discharge FROM open_meteo.main.flood_daily(52.52, 13.41) ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: Next 3 days.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, river_discharge FROM open_meteo.main.flood_daily(52.52, 13.41, forecast_days := 3) ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: The past 7 days instead of the forecast window.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT date, river_discharge FROM open_meteo.main.flood_daily(52.52, 13.41, past_days := 7, forecast_days := 0) ORDER BY date

vgi.example_queries.description: Many locations in one query — coordinates supplied by a column.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT c.city, w.date, w.river_discharge FROM (VALUES ('Berlin', 52.52, 13.41), ('Tokyo', 35.69, 139.69)) AS c(city, lat, lon), LATERAL open_meteo.main.flood_daily(c.lat, c.lon) AS w

vgi.example_queries.description: Daily river-discharge / flood forecast for a coordinate, starting from the place name 'Berlin' instead of a coordinate.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT g.name, w.date, w.river_discharge FROM open_meteo.main.geocoding('Berlin', count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.flood_daily(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w ORDER BY w.date

vgi.example_queries.description: A column of place names geocoded and queried in one pass.
vgi.example_queries.sql: SELECT p.city, w.date, w.river_discharge FROM (VALUES ('Berlin'), ('Tokyo')) AS p(city), LATERAL open_meteo.main.geocoding(p.city, count := 1) AS g, LATERAL open_meteo.main.flood_daily(g.latitude, g.longitude) AS w
